name: mmBERT (small/base) and EuroBERT (210m/610m/2.1B)
links: mmBERT: paper arXiv:2509.06888 (Marone et al., JHU CLSP); HF jhu-clsp/mmBERT-small, jhu-clsp/mmBERT-base; code github.com/JHU-CLSP/mmBERT; blog huggingface.co/blog/mmbert. EuroBERT: paper arXiv:2503.05500 (Boizard et al.); HF EuroBERT/EuroBERT-210m, EuroBERT/EuroBERT-610m, EuroBERT/EuroBERT-2.1B; code github.com/Nicolas-BZRD/EuroBERT; blog huggingface.co/blog/EuroBERT/release
license_access: Both open-weight. mmBERT: MIT (GitHub repo badge). EuroBERT: Apache 2.0; loading requires trust_remote_code=True (custom modeling code on the Hub).
track_coverage: mmBERT: T1 EN, T2 ES, T3 EU, T4 mixed (single multilingual model can serve all four tracks and all 12 mixed views). EuroBERT: T1 EN, T2 ES and the EN-ES / ES-EN mixed views only; Basque is not among its 15 training languages, so it is not a sensible choice for T3 or any EU-containing T4 view.
basque_quality: mmBERT: Basque (eus) is included, but only from the mid-training phase (110 languages) onward: 0 tokens in the 2.3T pre-training phase, ~1.4B tokens (0.23%) in mid-training and ~0.4B in each decay variant, ~2.6B tokens total (paper Appendix D, Table 9). Spanish gets ~123B tokens by comparison. No Basque-specific benchmark (XNLIeu, BasqueGLUE) is reported in the mmBERT paper [uncertain: none found]; its low-resource evidence is FoQA (Faroese) and TiQuaD (Tigrinya), where late-annealed languages still gain strongly. Tokenizer is Gemma 2 (256k vocab), which handles Basque reasonably. EuroBERT: Basque not covered (languages: English, French, German, Spanish, Chinese, Italian, Russian, Polish, Portuguese, Japanese, Vietnamese, Dutch, Arabic, Turkish, Hindi); Llama-3 tokenizer (128k) will over-fragment Basque; expect near mBERT-level or worse Basque performance [uncertain].
cross_lingual_robustness: mmBERT: shared multilingual space with strong XNLI cross-lingual transfer (77.7 avg XNLI for base, above XLM-R base) suggests a moderate gap between monolingual and mixed-language pairs; EN-ES mixed should be close to monolingual, EU-containing mixed pairs likely lose more because Basque was seen only in the last ~700B tokens [uncertain: no measured mixed-pair numbers]. EuroBERT: EN-ES mixed pairs should be fine (both well covered); any pair with a Basque side will degrade sharply because one side is effectively out-of-distribution.
architecture: Both are modern encoder-only transformers with RoPE, 8,192-token context and Flash-Attention support. mmBERT: ModernBERT recipe (22 layers, 1152 intermediate dim for base, alternating local/global attention, unpadding), Gemma 2 tokenizer, 3T+ tokens with cascading annealed language learning (60 -> 110 -> 1833 languages), inverse mask-ratio schedule (30% -> 15% -> 5%), final TIES merge of three decay variants. EuroBERT: Llama-style encoder (bidirectional attention, grouped-query attention, RMSNorm, RoPE), Llama-3 tokenizer, 4.8T pre-training tokens + 200B annealing tokens over 15 languages plus math and code. For DiCo, both are used as cross-encoders: [CLS]/pooled representation of '<phrase_a> [SEP] <phrase_b>' -> 4-way linear head.
params: mmBERT-small 140M (42M non-embedding); mmBERT-base 307M (110M non-embedding). EuroBERT-210m, EuroBERT-610m, EuroBERT-2.1B.
compute: Inputs are short phrase pairs (<64 tokens), so compute is trivial for the small models: mmBERT-small/base and EuroBERT-210m/610m full fine-tuning fits easily in 24 GB (bf16, batch 32-64), a few minutes per epoch on ~3k rows (T1-T3) and ~10-20 min per epoch on 18k T4 rows. EuroBERT-2.1B full fine-tuning with AdamW needs ~35-40 GB of weights+optimizer state (bf16 + fp32 master) -> 40-80 GB GPU, or LoRA / 8-bit Adam to fit 24 GB [uncertain]. mmBERT requires transformers >= 4.48 (ModernBERT support); EuroBERT requires trust_remote_code and a compatible transformers version.
sample_efficiency: With ~1.3k reversible source pairs (3042 rows per monolingual track) neither model has a public NLI-tuned checkpoint to start from [uncertain], so training directly from the MLM checkpoint on DiCo data alone will be data-starved and seed-sensitive (typical for 4-way NLI heads from scratch: several F1 points of seed variance). Strongly recommended: intermediate fine-tuning on MNLI/XNLI (+ XNLIeu machine-translated train for Basque, + Spanish XNLI) before DiCo, and run 3-5 seeds. ModernBERT-family models are known to be somewhat learning-rate sensitive; mmBERT paper sweeps LR in {2e-5..8e-5}; EuroBERT model card recommends 3.6e-5 (210m/610m) and 2.8e-5 (2.1B) for XNLI with warmup 0.1, weight decay 0.1.
reported_results: mmBERT (arXiv:2509.06888): XNLI avg accuracy mmBERT-small 75.8, mmBERT-base 77.7 vs EuroBERT-210m 71.9 (Table 7; HF blog quotes 77.1 vs XLM-R base 74.6); XTREME avg mmBERT-base 72.8 vs XLM-R base 70.4; GLUE MNLI mmBERT-small 85.8, mmBERT-base 87.7 vs XLM-R base 85.0, mGTE base 85.3; Arabic XNLI mmBERT 74.5 vs EuroBERT-210m 66.8. EuroBERT (arXiv:2503.05500, Table 1, XNLI averaged over its European languages): EuroBERT-210m 79.95, EuroBERT-610m 84.72, EuroBERT-2.1B 86.81 vs XLM-RoBERTa-280M 82.04, XLM-RoBERTa-560M 84.13, XLM-RoBERTa-3.5B 86.12. No XNLIeu, phrase-level NLI or DiCo numbers exist for either model [uncertain: none found].
pilot_dico_results: Not evaluated. The LREC 2026 pilot ('Assessing Logical Consistency in Fine-Grained NLI') covered English only; best system DeBERTa-v3-base (W-F1 0.75 / SoftCons 0.84 / HardCons 0.79); encoder-only family average 0.713 / 0.770 / 0.721, which is the most relevant prior for these encoders.
consistency_guarantee: none (plain 4-way classifier; consistency must come from joint pair decoding, antisymmetric heads or consistency loss applied on top)
negative_other_handling: NEGATIVE_OTHER is one of four softmax classes learned from data; nothing prevents the model from emitting NEG for one direction of a reversible pair and FE/BE/EQ for the other, which breaks SoftCons/HardCons. Recommended: pair-level NEG gate (average/max of p(NEG) over both directions and all language views) plus joint decoding over consistent label pairs.
metric_tradeoff: As single models, expect W-F1 roughly in the encoder-family range (pilot 0.71 avg on EN) on T1/T2, with SoftCons/HardCons similar to other encoders unless joint decoding is added. mmBERT should be competitive with XLM-R base-size on T3/T4 but probably below XLM-R-large / RoBERTa-euscrawl-large [uncertain]. EuroBERT-2.1B may give a W-F1 gain on T1/T2 (XNLI on par with XLM-R-XL) but adds nothing on Basque. Consistency metrics are governed mainly by the decoding/method layer, not by the backbone choice.
integration: mmBERT: AutoModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained('jhu-clsp/mmBERT-base', num_labels=4, id2label=ID2LABEL, label2id=LABEL2ID) (ModernBertForSequenceClassification) - drop-in with the existing HF pipeline; enable flash-attn/unpadding for speed. EuroBERT: AutoModelForSequenceClassification with trust_remote_code=True (EuroBERT remote code provides a sequence-classification class [uncertain about pooling defaults]); pin the Hub revision for reproducibility. Both output logits for the 4 labels in src/labels.py order; reversal aggregation via REVERSE_PERM works unchanged.
ensemble_compatibility: Yes - softmax over 4 classes; calibrate with temperature scaling on dev before log-prob pooling across views/directions.
inference_cost: Negligible: ~4k test rows x 2 directions x views labels in well under a minute on one GPU for base-size models; a few minutes for EuroBERT-2.1B.
rules_disclosure: Disclose: open-weight; encoder-only (ModernBERT-style for mmBERT, Llama-style bidirectional encoder for EuroBERT); fine-tuned; any intermediate NLI data used (MNLI/XNLI/XNLIeu etc.) as external training data; ensembling if combined. Licenses (MIT / Apache 2.0) are unproblematic.
contamination: Pretraining corpora are web-scale (mmBERT: FineWeb2, DCLM, Dolma-style sources; EuroBERT: FineWeb/CulturaX-style multilingual web + code/math) and could contain the public English iSTS/PhrasIS source sentences (SemEval-2016 iSTS headlines/images), but not the DiCo labels or the new ES/EU translations; risk is low and unlabeled [uncertain]. Main contamination risk comes from any intermediate fine-tuning on PhrasIS/iSTS - must respect the pending PhrasIS policy and the test split grouped by source pair.
structural_cue_dependence: No - the model sees only the two phrases; any pair_id / singleton-NEG heuristics live in the decoding layer and are optional.
priority: mmBERT-base: P1 (multilingual challenger/ensemble member for T3/T4 alongside XLM-R-large); EuroBERT: P2 (only for T1/T2 and EN-ES mixed views; 2.1B worth a try only if compute is spare).
expected_gain: mmBERT-base: modest; it beats XLM-R base on XNLI/MNLI and covers Basque, so it is a cheap, fast, diverse ensemble member for T3/T4, but at 307M it is unlikely to beat XLM-R-large or dedicated Basque large encoders on its own [uncertain]. EuroBERT: potential +1-3 W-F1 on T1/T2 from the 2.1B model relative to base-size encoders, but English DeBERTa-v3-large NLI checkpoints and Spanish/XLM-R-large NLI checkpoints are stronger known quantities; no value for Basque.
